# Widening as what every weighting ranks

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`widening-as-what-every-weighting-ranks` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F07 · [record](widening-as-what-every-weighting-ranks.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Over a finite listing, one course widens another exactly when every order ranking each widening higher ranks it higher, additive or not, as every positive weighting does; a mixed comparison is decided both ways; a zero weight ties; one weight for all ranks by number.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Over a finite listing of items, a course is the items it admits and a weighting gives each a natural weight. Inclusion never lowers a weighted count, and every weighting positive on every item ranks a widening strictly higher. (`Becoming.Weighting.weighed`, `Becoming.Weighting.Positive`, `Becoming.Weighting.weighed_le_of_includes`, `Becoming.Weighting.weighed_lt_of_widens`)
2. Where one course admits a listed item the other does not, some positive weighting ranks it higher; so a mixed comparison is decided both ways by positive weightings. (`Becoming.Weighting.outweighing`, `Becoming.Weighting.outweighs`, `Becoming.Weighting.mixed_either_way`)
3. On the listed items one course widens another exactly when every positive weighting ranks it higher. (`Becoming.Weighting.widens_iff_every_positive`)
4. Additivity is not needed: for any class of orders from the positive weightings up to every order ranking each widening higher (priority to the worse off among them), one course widens another exactly when every order of the class ranks it higher, every complete order included, and within each class a mixed comparison is decided both ways; on a web, the same of what level paths admit. (`Becoming.Weighting.Increasing`, `Becoming.Weighting.ranks`, `Becoming.Weighting.increasing_ranks`, `Becoming.Weighting.widens_iff_every_of_class`, `Becoming.Weighting.widens_iff_every_increasing`, `Becoming.Weighting.widens_iff_every_score`, `Becoming.Weighting.mixed_either_way_of_class`, `Becoming.Weighting.increasing_prior`, `Becoming.Web.widens_iff_every_of_class`)
5. Where every item a course admits beyond another weighs nothing, the two weigh the same: a weighting that leaves an item out does not rank a widening that adds only that item. (`Becoming.Weighting.weighed_eq_of_unweighted`)
6. Under one positive weight for every item, a course weighs more exactly when it admits more items. (`Becoming.Weighting.weighed_const`, `Becoming.Weighting.neutral_ranks_by_number`)
7. On a web, where admission is decided and what either level path admits is listed, one path widens the other exactly when every weighting positive on the listed steps and formations ranks it higher. (`Becoming.Web.DecidesAdmission`, `Becoming.Web.ListsAdmitted`, `Becoming.Web.widens_iff_every_weighting`)
8. Where one level path admits a formation at a step and another does not, the other neither widens nor keeps it: the comparison never ranks the course in which something is closed above the one in which it is not. (`Becoming.Web.not_widens_of_closes`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom. Finite listings of items (steps and formations); admission two-valued (Bool) and, on webs, decided; weights natural numbers; for the weighted laws a standpoint's order represented as an additive weighting, supplied, not derived; for the class laws only that each order of the class ranks every widening higher and that the class holds the positive weightings' orders.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- That a standpoint's order ranks every widening higher (monotone, counting every item), or which order a standpoint has.
- That the impartial order is what every standpoint shares rather than one privileged weighting, or that widening is better: calling widening better is C, a premise.
- Graded significance, chance, or magnitude beyond counting listed items; partiality outside mixed comparisons is not excluded for weightings that are not positive.
- **Counterexample:** For a mixed pair, the weighting giving the items one course admits beyond the other more weight than the other's whole listing (Weighting.outweighing) ranks it higher, and the swapped weighting the other way (Weighting.mixed_either_way): no positive weighting is forced on a mixed comparison. <details><summary>Correspondence, dependencies, sources and history</summary>

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Sen's intersection approach (Collective Choice and Social Welfare, 1970; "On Weights and Measures", 1977): the judgments every weighting in a set shares form a quasi-ordering; any quasi-ordering is an intersection of orderings (Donaldson and Weymark 1998). In multi-objective optimization, dominance in every coordinate is ranking by every positive weighted sum, here the finite 0/1 case. The inclusion order with strict monotonicity on opportunity sets is Pattanaik and Xu (1990). The reading places Scheffler's agent-centred prerogative (1982) and Williams's partiality (1976) in exactly the mixed comparisons, and Taurek's question (1977) at the equal weighting.

<a id="dependencies--依赖"></a>
### Dependencies

- **formal-reuse**: [comparison-by-widening](comparison-by-widening.md). Reuses the comparison by widening on webs (Web.Widens, Web.Keeps, Web.Admits).
  - Output: One level path widens another where it admits at every step what the other admits and at some step more.
  - Input: Widening as what every positive weighting of the listed admissions ranks higher.
  - Preserved conditions: Admission decided; what either path admits listed. [Regions.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Regions.lean)
- related, not a proved adapter: [what-the-step-across-standpoints-reaches](what-the-step-across-standpoints-reaches.md). The same section's scope: what the step of invariance reaches across standpoints.
- related, not a proved adapter: [protection-priority-excludes-uniform-aggregation](protection-priority-excludes-uniform-aggregation.md). A priority of basic conditions is a lexical order no natural-number score represents; such an order is not one of the weightings here, and it can decide comparisons the shared order leaves mixed.
